summary: P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD under Eliot Deutsch). He served at Ceylon (as Pali and Buddhist Studies head, 1997–2004) and later as Emeritus Professor at PIPBS.
P. H. Joshi is an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1976–1988, 2002).
P. K. Mukhopadhyay worked in philosophy and Indology. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under A. Chinnaswami Sastri. He worked at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1941) and served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1967).

Pramod P. Joglekar works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the Regulating Council of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and as Professor of Bioarchaeology at Deccan College (attested 2026).

P. P. Subrahmanya Sastri studied Indology at the University of Madras and University of Oxford. He served as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Chennai.
P. Pratap Kumar works in religious studies and Indology. He held posts as Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (attested 2010) and Visiting Professor at Colorado College (attested 2010).
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who pursued Ph.D. studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri studied at Bishop Heber College and the University of Madras. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he was Principal of Rajah's College (1932–1942) and Head of Sanskrit at Annamalai University (1942–1947).
P. Swaminathan, an Indologist, completed an M.Litt. at the University of Madras under V. Raghavan. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at National Sanskrit University (attested 1965).
P. T. Narasimhachar was an Indology scholar who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1923–1926) under Mysore Hiriyanna.
P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indologist who served as Director of the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute (attested 1944, 1954).
Padma Subrahmanyam is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Stella Maris College, Ethiraj College for Women, and Annamalai University (~1974–1979) under T. N. Ramachandran.
Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who served as Professor (attested 1977–1990, 2002) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2016) at the University of California, Berkeley.

Palmira Brummett, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at Chicago and Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She was professor emeritus at the University of Tennessee (~1988–2011) and visiting professor at Brown (2011–2016).
Palmo Kyi is a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Per Kværne (supervisor attested 2012), Hanna Havnevik, and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna and was a research student at the Australian National University (~1972–1976).

Pandurang Vaman Kane studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. An Indologist and historian, he held law and Sanskrit teaching posts, served at the Bombay High Court, and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).
Pankaj Tandon works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under mentor Tom Mallon-McCorgray and held a post at Boston University (attested 2015).
